newsitem.title: UK: Britain to allow pools on midweek soccer.
newsitem.headline: Britain to allow pools on midweek soccer.

text.p: The British government announced on Tuesday it will drop regulations which prevented football pools companies from running competitions on midweek matches.
But Home Office Minister Timothy Kirkhope said it had dropped the idea of allowing pools competitions on horseracing.

Pools companies, led by Littlewoods, Ladbroke Group Plc unit Vernons, and Zetters Group Plc, have been pressing for deregulation of their industry to help them fight back against competition from the National Lottery.
Under present laws, the companies are able to offer pools only on games played at weekends and public holidays.
"I have decided to remove this requirement as it serves no useful purpose and is an unnecessary restriction to pool promoters and their customers," Kirkhope said in a statement.
He also said he had on Monday relaxed the rules on rollovers in pools competitions. They had previously been allowed only on weeks when the National Lottery had a similar rollover.
Kirkhope said he also planned to change the law to allow the payment of pools winnings in shops.
However he added: "The proposal which would allow shops, pubs, clubs and other premises to sell pools competitions on horseracing will not be taken forward.
"This is due to concerns that it could change the pools into a harder form of gambling with frequent opportunities to place bets and chase losses."
It was not clear if the new measures would come into force before the end of the current parliamentary session.
